content.content:
An id listed in one of the detail panel's four relationship sections (rmovtvkt) that names a node document shows the pointer cursor: while the pointer is over that entry, the cursor is the pointing hand a browser shows over a link, not the text cursor the same characters would otherwise take. The entry is a run of characters — the selected node's field value, shown as the bare id (mwwxxzyk) — so its cursor is what the reader reads before committing to a click; the hand says the entry is something to point at and press, and it says so before the reader tries.

The cue accompanies the pointer click that kwxutvpw fixed as one of the two ways to activate a listed id, and it is the pointer's half of the entry's presentation. It is not a claim about the other input: this decision says nothing about keyboard reachability, focusability, focus order or what marks the entry while it has focus, and a hand cursor tells no reader that the entry can be reached from the keyboard. Nor does the cue stand in for the activation: showing it is not pressing the entry, and what a click does, where the selection goes and what the panel then shows are kwxutvpw's and rusopkql's, unchanged.

The cue appears on every listed entry that names a node, in all four sections alike, and whether the id names a decision or an evaluation — an evaluation's id is an entry that follows to its node exactly as a decision's does (mwwxxzyk). Nothing else in the panel gains the cue from this decision: an id the panel mentions outside a relationship section — inside the selected node's kind, content or rationale text, on the canvas, in a section's empty state — is not a listed entry, and the entry that names no node is not covered here at all.

An id that names no node document is the case rusopkql settled as listed but inert, whose appearance both that decision and mwwxxzyk left to the appearance records. This decision does not take it. Whether the entry that cannot be followed shows the pointer cursor, a cue of another kind or no cue is settled where the inert entry's presentation is decided, and nothing here requires that entry to match the entry that names a node, or to differ from it. The cue for the followable entry is stated as a fact about that entry, not as a rule over every listed id, so that the inert entry's cue stays a decision of its own rather than an exception carved out here.

The cue is one property and stops there. This decision does not say which colour role the entry takes, whether it is underlined, what else the entry does under the pointer besides the cursor, what marks it while it has focus, or which element and which class vocabulary carry the cue: the colour role, the hover treatment, the focus outline, the inert entry's role and the entry vocabulary are each a separate commitment, and none of them is fixed, required, forbidden or implied here. It names no class, adds no style property, rule or stylesheet of its own, and places the cue in no file. It fixes the cue and the entries that show it; the carriers that draw the entry implement it, and it holds there whatever element and vocabulary they use. The canvas is outside it: the cursor over a node or an edge, and the size of any target drawn there, are not touched, restated or narrowed here, so the recorded hit-target value for those elements stands exactly as it was.
content.rationale:
mwwxxzyk committed a listed entry to reading as a link and then stopped before the cue that a reader meets first: it named the pointer cursor among the parts it did not decide, so as the panel stands a followable id carries no cursor that distinguishes it from the prose beside it, and the reader who points at one is told nothing until the click. Of the cues that index a link — a colour, an underline, a cursor, a focus ring, a vocabulary — the cursor is the smallest and the most specific: it needs no colour role, no decoration, no extra element and no class name, it changes no text and no geometry, and it is the one cue that appears exactly where the reader is deciding whether to press. Spending one cue leaves the other four open for their own records, which is why this is its own unit rather than a clause inside the link decision.

wtywxppt records one hit-target value for the canvas elements it names, with a note that carries two things at once: pointer precision and keyboard reachability. This entry is a detail-panel entry, so the licence it draws from that record is the pointer-precision commitment in its note and rationale — an interactive element that the pointer can reliably find and target — and the pointer cursor is that commitment made visible before the click. The keyboard half stays where it is: whether the entry is reachable from the keyboard, whether it takes focus, and what marks it then are separate records, and the entry's activation already fixes its keyboard inputs without this decision's help. Fixing the pointer cue and abstaining from the keyboard is not a narrowing of the prerequisite — nothing here forbids or removes a keyboard route — and it is not a claim that the pointer user is the user who matters; it is one record taking one half of a note so that the other half is not claimed twice. Nor does the cue take wtywxppt's measurement: the recorded value is a hit-target floor for the canvas, and the size of an entry's target is settled where the entry's geometry is drawn, so nothing here sizes, pads or extends the entry, and the cue is not asserted to be a target of any particular size.

Leaving the inert entry out is deliberate and is the part most at risk of being closed by accident, because a cursor property applies to whatever is pointed at. rusopkql kept the id that names no node listed and inert, and both it and mwwxxzyk explicitly left that entry's look to the appearance decisions. Stating the cue for the entry that names a node, as a fact about that entry rather than as a rule over every listed id, leaves the entry that cannot be followed free to be presented as the different case it may honestly be, and spares the next decision an exception it never chose. By the same restraint the cue carries no colour, no underline and no focus marker: those are the other units' properties, and fixing any of them here would either duplicate or contradict a record that owns it. The decision stays in words because it decides a cue, not a rendering: the stylesheet and the panel are the carriers, gated where those artifacts are read, and this record is what they implement.
